angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 200,362 km at 63.00 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.8734 +/- 0.0343 mas (same row, RUWE 1.20): 63.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.288 +/- 0.028 solar radii from Hirano et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-28 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract): 200,362 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.257 +/- 0.048 solar masses from Hirano et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-28 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3214 +/- 60 K from Hirano et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-28 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hirano et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-28 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-28.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.929, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-28 (pscomppars): spectral type M4, from Hirano et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, LP 700-6: main object type LM*, Low-mass Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-28 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.26 dex, from Hirano et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...820...41H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-28 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.9397, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
